target_customer: Commercial real estate brokerages and brokers doing phone prospecting
problem: Brokers make many cold calls that go to voicemail, and generic voicemails rarely earn callbacks.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat for a calling and data platform
product_category: AI power dialer and CRE data platform

founders.name: Vincent Wilson
prior_employers: Palantir (incoming forward deployed software engineer, did not start)
education: University of Washington, computer science, dropped out

education: University of Pennsylvania, Wharton and Penn Engineering
founders.background_notes: Built an ML stock prediction model as a senior.

founders.name: Gabriel Wilson

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice cloning, telephony and dialer infrastructure are mostly assembled from third party components, with integration and compliance challenges.

defensibility.rationale: Voicemail drop and AI voice features are available across many dialers; any edge comes from CRE specific data and broker workflow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Generic dialers added AI voicemail features (found only in undated 2025 and 2026 pages), so the wedge was crowded later.

market_need_then: Brokers rely on cold calling and voicemail callbacks; company copy says its first customers are CRE brokerages. No dated demand data was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct and benefit focused, for example 'No call is cold with Terrakotta.ai'.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches for the name returned only unrelated terracotta businesses, and the K spelling is easy to confuse with the common word.

pivots.from: AI voicemail power dialer for brokers
pivots.to: CRE data and calling platform (Dial plus property database)
pivots.why: Not stated; the site now shows property data, owner research and skip tracing beside the dialer.

outcome_analysis: Terrakotta is an active Winter 2024 company that started as an AI voicemail dialer and now sells a CRE calling and data platform with named brokerage logos on its site. No shutdown or acquisition news was found, and outside funding is unclear, so the stage of its growth is unknown.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (CB Insights, VCBacked, Extruct) show about 500K around 2024-02 from Y Combinator and 1984 Ventures, labelled pre-seed, seed or convertible note; Latka claims no outside funding and about 330K 2025 revenue with 3 people, an estimate. No press coverage found so no round recorded. Competitor search returned only undated vendor pages, so the list is empty. Customer logos on the site (Cushman and Wakefield, CBRE, Lee and Associates, Avison Young) are self reported. Pivot dating is unknown. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed of 2024-02 is recorded from VCBacked; 1984 Ventures appears only on Extruct. Latka claims no outside funding (conflict). Single database basis; no press found.
